## Combo 1916-1938-1971
Cards: Yannik, Scavenging Sentinel + Changeling Titan + Glorious Protector
Color identity: GW | Bracket: 3-4+ (Spicy) | Popularity: 28 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {0} plus the mana cost of the creature in your hand
Produces: Infinite +1/+1 counters on creatures you control; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature LTB
Start: Yannik, Scavenging Sentinel (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield); Changeling Titan (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield); Glorious Protector (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield)
Prerequisites: Glorious Protector must be exiled by Changeling Titan, and Yannik must begin in hand. (This starting order is not fixed, and their initial positions may be interchanged as necessary.)
Steps: Cast Yannik for its mana cost.
  When Yannik enters, it exiles Changeling Titan until Yannik leaves the battlefield. Resolve any additional effects of Yannik's ETB.
  When Changeling Titan leaves the battlefield, Glorious Protector is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  When Glorious Protector enters, it exiles Yannik until Glorious Protector leaves the battlefield. Resolve any additional effects of Glorious Protector's ETB.
  When Yannik leaves the battlefield, Changeling Titan is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  When Changeling Titan enters, it exiles Glorious Protector until Changeling Titan leaves the battlefield. Resolve any additional effects of Changeling Titan's ETB.
  When Glorious Protector leaves the battlefield, Yannik is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Due to differences in card templating between the various banisher effects (linked triggered abilities vs "until" clause), steps 3, 5, and 7 may return the creature to the battlefield during the resolution of the preceding step rather than creating a separate event. This should not affect the overall execution of the combo, only how many objects pass through the stack (and thus rounds of priority available per loop).

  When Lumbering Battlement leaves the battlefield, Changeling Titan is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Due to differences in card templating between the various banisher effects (linked triggered abilities vs "until" clause), steps 3, 5, and 7 may return the creature to the battlefield during the resolution of the preceding step rather than creating a separate event. This should not affect the overall execution of the combo, only how many objects pass through the stack (and thus rounds of priority available per loop).

## Combo 2034-3234-3293-5413
Cards: Emeria Shepherd + World Shaper + Ashnod's Altar + Trenching Steed
Color identity: GW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal
Produces: Infinite self-mill; Infinite colorless mana; Infinite creature LTB; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Infinite death triggers; Infinite landfall triggers; Return all nonland permanents from your graveyard to the battlefield
Start: Emeria Shepherd (battlefield); World Shaper (battlefield); Ashnod's Altar (battlefield); Trenching Steed (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You control a Plains or have a Plains in your graveyard.
Steps: Activate Trenching Steed by sacrificing a land.
  Repeat step 1 until you control no lands.
  Activate Ashnod's Altar by sacrificing World Shaper.
  When World Shaper dies, it triggers, return all lands from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped.
  When the lands enter, Emeria Shepherd triggers that many times.
  Resolve an Emeria Shepherd trigger that was triggered by a Plains, returning World Shaper from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Resolve all remaining Emeria Shepherd triggers.
  Repeat
Notes: You can return all nonland permanents in your graveyard and library to the battlefield if you control there are two or more Plains between your graveyard, library and battlefield. To do this, have all triggers from Emeria Shepherd target desired permanents. Then, resolve the Plains triggers first to return those cards to the battlefield, causing all other triggers to fizzle on the stack.

## Combo 3234-3293-3899-5413
Cards: Emeria Shepherd + World Shaper + Spawning Pit + Trenching Steed
Color identity: GW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal
Produces: Infinite self-mill; Infinite charge counters on a permanent; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature LTB; Infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Infinite death triggers; Infinite landfall triggers; Return all nonland permanents from your graveyard to the battlefield
Start: Emeria Shepherd (battlefield); World Shaper (battlefield); Spawning Pit (battlefield); Trenching Steed (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You control a Plains or have a Plains in your graveyard.
Steps: Activate Trenching Steed by sacrificing a land.
  Repeat step 1 until you control no lands.
  Activate Spawning Pit by sacrificing World Shaper.
  When World Shaper dies, it triggers, return all lands from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped.
  When the lands enter, Emeria Shepherd triggers that many times.
  Resolve an Emeria Shepherd trigger that was triggered by a Plains, returning World Shaper from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Resolve all remaining Emeria Shepherd triggers.
  Resolve the Spawning Pit ability.
  Repeat
Notes: You can return all nonland permanents in your graveyard and library to the battlefield if you control there are two or more Plains between your graveyard, library and battlefield. To do this, have all triggers from Emeria Shepherd target desired permanents. Then, resolve the Plains triggers first to return those cards to the battlefield, causing all other triggers to fizzle on the stack.

Prerequisites: You control a Plains or have a Plains in your graveyard.
  You do not have any static effects boosting your creatures' toughness.
Steps: Cast Lumra by paying {4}{G}{G}.
  When Lumra enters, it triggers.
  Holding priority, activate Sylvan Safekeeper by sacrificing a land.
  Repeat step 3 until you control no lands.
  When you sacrifice the last land, Lumra will die as a state-based action due to having 0 toughness.
  Resolve the Lumra trigger from step 2, causing you to mill four cards and return all lands from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped.
  When the lands enter, Emeria Shepherd triggers that many times.
  Resolve an Emeria Shepherd trigger that was triggered by a Plains, returning Lumra from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: You can return all nonland permanents in your graveyard and library to the battlefield if you control there are two or more Plains between your graveyard, library and battlefield. To do this, have all triggers from Emeria Shepherd target desired permanents. Then, resolve the Plains triggers first to return those cards to the battlefield, causing all other triggers to fizzle on the stack.

## Combo 3778-7299

Color identity: GW | Bracket: 3+ (Powerful) | Popularity: 250 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {10}{G}{G}{W}{W}

Start: Biorhythm (hand); Austere Command (hand)
Steps: Cast Austere Command by paying its mana cost, destroying all creatures.
  Cast Biorhythm by paying its mana cost, causing each player's life total to become equal to the number of creatures they control.

## Combo 6441-6753-7858
Cards: Hollowhenge Overlord + Elspeth, Storm Slayer + Exalted Sunborn
Color identity: GW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 53 | Commander: legal
Produces: Near-infinite creature tokens; Near-infinite creature ETB
Start: Hollowhenge Overlord (battlefield); Elspeth, Storm Slayer (battlefield); Exalted Sunborn (battlefield)
Steps: At the beginning of your upkeep, Hollowhenge Overlord triggers, creating four 2/2 Wolf creature tokens for each Wolf and/or Werewolf you control due to Elspeth, Storm Slayer and Exalted Sunborn.
  Repeat step 1 during each of your upkeeps. You'll create exponentially more Wolves each time assuming the Wolf tokens survive.
Notes: The number of Wolves and/or Werewolves you'll control after performing steps 1 and 2 is equal to 5^X * Y, where X is the number of iterations of those steps you've performed (starting at 1), and Y is the initial number of Wolves and/or Werewolves you started with. So if you start with 6 creatures, you'll have 30 after the first iteration, 150 after the second, and so on. This also assumes no Wolves and/or Werewolves die, and no more are created during the turns.
